conflicts: 6s 2[2]5/2 (54633.28 cm^-1) lifetime: 195(29) ns (Spietz et al. 2001, adopted by NIST: A = 5.14e6 s^-1) versus 80(30) ns (Lawrence 1967, Table 6; 90(30) ns in Table 7 of the same paper) and 78(5) ns (CI-MBPT, Filin et al. 2020). Filin et al. state that the two measurements differ by more than a factor of two and that their theory agrees with Lawrence. Unresolved.
6p 2[1]°3/2 (67061.96 cm^-1) lifetime: 35.5(9) ns (Esteves et al. 2023, TALIF) versus 39(2) ns (Kono & Hattori 1979; +4/-8 with systematics) versus 32.5(1.2) ns (CI-MBPT). Esteves value adopted.

2P1/2 lifetime / A(1315 nm): post-1980 measurements 0.127(3), 0.130(7), 0.125(6), 0.1077(12), 0.145(40) s (Filin Table IV) and outliers 0.0257, 0.0484, 0.1116, 0.1372 s (Chichinin Table 1); the uncertainty of the Engleman value is printed as +-6 ms by Filin and +-0.025 s by Chichinin. NIST adopts A = 8.0 s^-1 (accuracy C). Filin's Table IV header gives the unit as 1e-6 s, which is a misprint for 1e-3 s.
A(2P1/2) hyperfine constant: 6625(90) MHz (Zuev et al. 1972, Chichinin Table 2) versus 6587(4) MHz derived from the FT hyperfine levels of Luc-Koenig et al. 1973; the FT-derived value is adopted.

level energies: Esteves et al. 2023 shift all excited I I levels by -0.169(11) cm^-1 with respect to NIST ASD 5.9 (e.g. 67062.130 -> 67061.961); the cached NIST table (67061.9638, 65669.8213, 54633.2819) already includes this revision, older papers (Filin, Marmuse) use the unshifted energies.
not_found: measured Einstein A values / relative strengths of the individual hyperfine components of the 1315 nm line (Ha et al., Ber. Bunsenges. Phys. Chem. 99, 384 (1995); He et al.): not accessible; the components are given with angular-momentum-derived fractions only (flagged derived).
radiative lifetime of the 304.67 nm TALIF upper level 6p 2[3]°5/2 (65644.311 cm^-1) and of 6p 2[3]°7/2 (65669.82 cm^-1): no measurement located.

hyperfine A, B constants of the remaining I I levels (37 even and 42 odd levels in Luc-Koenig, Morillon, Verges, Phys. Scr. 12, 199 (1975); Deng et al., JQSRT 161, 153 (2015); Ashok et al., JQSRT 205, 19 (2018); Mu et al., JQSRT 217, 229 (2018)): IOP and Elsevier full texts not accessible; only the two levels quoted in the Esteves thesis are recorded (6s 2[2]5/2 and 6p 2[3]°7/2).
measured Lande g factor of the ground level 2P°3/2 (blank in the NIST table) and measured g factors beyond NIST: none located in an openable source.
isotope shifts: 127I is the only stable isotope; no 129I data sought or located.

Walter et al., Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. 35, 095010 (2026) (TALIF at 298.2 nm with photolysis reference; open access but behind the IOP bot wall): only the Crossref abstract was read; it gives the scheme (298.2 nm, fluorescence 804.6 nm) and no atomic constants.

measured transition probabilities of the visible / near-infrared 6s-6p lines newer than NIST: none located (Filin et al. 2020 give CI-MBPT values only; Baklanov et al. 1997 VUV values are already the NIST ones).

second pass (2026-10-01): no further open source with measured I I data was found. Kono & Hattori, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 69, 253 (1979) measured only three 6p levels of I I (all three are already in this file); the hyperfine papers of Luc-Koenig et al. (1975), Deng et al. (2015), Ashok et al. (2018, 2019) and Mu et al. (2018) remain closed (Elsevier / IOP), no thesis or preprint copy located.

Einstein A of the 1315 nm line by diode-laser absorption, (6.95 +- 1.65) s^-1 (Ha et al. 1995), is quoted by Esteves et al. 2024 (hal-04429627); it is the 0.145(40) s lifetime already listed under conflicts.
notes: Literature search was limited: the session's web-search quota was exhausted, so sources were located through Crossref, HAL, OSTI, arXiv and NASA ADS queries and only open copies could be read (IOP, Elsevier, APS full texts were not accessible). Hyperfine constants: Casimir convention E = A*C/2 + B*[3C(C+1) - 4I(I+1)J(J+1)]/[8I(2I-1)J(2J-1)] with C = F(F+1) - I(I+1) - J(J+1), I = 5/2; the Luc-Koenig constants are quoted second-hand in 1e-3 cm^-1 and converted to MHz here. Two-photon entries: wavelength_vac_nm is the laser wavelength and frequency_THz the two-photon sum frequency (level energy), both for hyperfine barycentres. Air wavelengths of the fluorescence lines (804.4, 905.8, 911.4 nm) are as printed by Esteves et al. The extra keys energy_cm, quenching, E2_to_M1_ratio, absorption_cross_section and hyperfine_components are not in the schema and can be ignored by the pipeline. Second pass (2026-10-01): added use annotations for the three 6s-6p fluorescence lines of the TALIF schemes (no new numbers).
